newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Arafat offers to mediate in Kashmir dispute.
newsitem.headline: Arafat offers to mediate in Kashmir dispute.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat offered during a visit to Islamabad on Friday to mediate in the dispute between arch-foes Pakistan and India over the Himalayan region of Kashmir.

In an interview with state television after talks with Pakistani leaders, Arafat called Kashmiri people his brothers and said he hoped they would find an "accurate solution for what they have suffered".
"I am ready to return...to mediate to find the solution because they (Kashmiris) are my brothers," he said.
State media said that Arafat supported Islamabad's stand on Kashmir during his talks with Pakistan's acting president Wasim Sajjad and Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.

The Palestinian leader had arrived earlier on Friday from a visit to Japan and later left for Cairo, where he is to attend an emergency meeting of Arab foreign ministers called to seek a united stand on recent developments in Arab-Israeli relations.
New Delhi, which is fighting a separatist revolt in two-thirds of Kashmir it rules, regards the whole of the former princely state as an integral part of India.

But Islamabad, which controls the remaining third of the region, wants the predominantly Moslem Kashmiris to decide in a United Nations-mandated plebiscite whether to join Islamic Pakistan or Hindu-majority India.
Two of three wars between India and Pakistan since their independence from Britain in 1947 were fought over Kashmir.
